job: Preparing the next AI-generated Lean proof release so its stated warrant is an independent kernel re-check, not a clean axiom audit.
outcome: A published proof set whose release notes name a second, distinct checker at a patched toolchain as the guarantee.
motivation: A model-written formalisation has no second reader, so the checker is the only defence and one implementation is not enough.

task.who: lab formal-mathematics team and proof-artifact release engineering
task.what: Draft the release warrant around external re-checking
task.where: Proof repository release notes and artifact README
task.why: Axiom audits returned clean on a proof of False
task.how: External environment checker run over the exported proof environment

job: Hardening the Lean kernel after the wrong-structure projection bug and cutting patched toolchain releases that publishers can pin against.
outcome: A patched toolchain line, with stricter parameter validation, that an AI-proof release can cite as the version its re-check ran on.
motivation: A kernel that accepted a proof of False without axioms leaves every downstream certificate resting on an unproven implementation.

task.who: Lean core kernel and release-management maintainers
task.what: Add parameter validation for nested inductive auxiliary types
task.where: Lean 4 kernel typechecker and patch-release branches
task.why: Phantom parameters were dropped, letting ill-typed arguments through
task.how: Regression suite plus adversarial metaprogram declarations fed to the kernel

job: Keeping an external type checker able to consume full library-scale exported environments from current proof-assistant toolchains.
outcome: A second checker, written against the specification rather than forked from the kernel, that a publisher can run unattended.
motivation: A patched copy of one implementation shares that implementation's blind spots; only a distinct implementation can actually disagree.

task.who: external type-checker project maintainers and contributors
task.what: Track kernel changes and keep export ingestion current
task.where: Standalone checker repository and its conformance test suite
task.why: Only a distinct implementation can contradict the primary kernel
task.how: Specification-derived typechecker reading the environment export format

job: Wiring the second checker into the proof repository build so the re-check runs on every commit, not on the reader's machine.
outcome: A build job that exports the compiled environment and fails when the independent checker rejects any of the results.
motivation: The challenges directory hands verification to whoever clones the code, which is exactly where nobody is doing it.

task.who: release engineering and build infrastructure for the proof repository
task.what: Add an independent re-check stage to the pipeline
task.where: Repository continuous-integration workflow and aggregate build target
task.why: The publisher, not the reader, must find a disagreement
task.how: Lake build plus environment export piped to the external checker

job: Moving the shared library onto patched toolchain lines and keeping its exported environment stable enough to re-check whole.
outcome: A library release, on a fixed kernel, whose exported environment an independent checker can verify end to end.
motivation: Every AI-generated formalisation builds on this library, so its toolchain pin sets the floor for every certificate downstream.

task.who: library maintainers and toolchain bump reviewers
task.what: Bump the library past the fixed kernel release
task.where: Library master branch and toolchain bump pull requests
task.why: Certificates inherit whatever kernel the library was built against
task.how: Staged toolchain bump with full library rebuild and export check

job: Hunting further kernel-reachable unsoundness by minimising suspicious proofs and filing reproducible declarations against current nightlies.
outcome: A public record of further kernel-only holes that makes a single-implementation certificate untenable as a published warrant.
motivation: One bug reachable only from metaprograms already produced a clean axiom report sitting on a proof of False.

task.who: independent proof-assistant researchers and issue triagers
task.what: Minimise suspect proofs into reproducible kernel test cases
task.where: Proof-assistant issue tracker and nightly toolchain builds
task.why: Public counterexamples force publishers to name a second checker
task.how: Metaprogram-driven declaration fuzzing and proof-term minimisation

job: Rewriting artifact criteria so a machine-checked submission must document re-checking by an implementation distinct from the one that compiled it.
outcome: Submission guidelines that treat a build log and an axiom audit as insufficient evidence for a machine-generated proof.
motivation: Machine proofs arrive faster than referees can read them, so the venue's only remaining check is the checker itself.

task.what: Revise artifact criteria for machine-generated formal proofs
task.where: Conference call for artifacts and reviewer guidelines
task.why: No referee reads a model-written formalisation line by line
task.how: Reviewer checklist requiring a named second checker and its logs

job: Keeping the kernel-independent export format complete and current so an outside checker can re-derive the whole compiled environment.
outcome: An export path carrying every declaration a second checker needs, versioned against the patched toolchain releases.
motivation: Without a faithful export there is no way for a distinct implementation to re-check anything at all.

task.who: export tooling maintainers and kernel interface reviewers
task.what: Extend the export format to cover new kernel declarations
task.where: Export tooling and its round-trip conformance tests
task.why: A second checker can only read what the export emits
task.how: Round-trip tests exporting and re-importing full library environments

job: Reproducing headline machine-generated results in a proof assistant other than the one that produced them, from the statement down.
outcome: An independent re-derivation in a different prover that a publisher can cite instead of, or beside, an external kernel check.
motivation: Agreement between two unrelated provers is the strongest form of the disagreement test this prediction asks for.

task.who: formalisation researchers working in a second proof assistant
task.what: Re-formalise selected published results in another prover
task.where: Separate formalisation repository targeting a different proof assistant
task.why: Two unrelated implementations agreeing is a real independence check
task.how: Manual restatement plus proof porting across library ontologies
